lines.text: The masks found us two days later, on the river road, where the forest runs right up to the cliffs above the Senn.
Twelve riders in dark red armour, with iron half-masks shaped like the jaws of dogs. They came out of the trees ahead of us and behind us, without a sound.
Lucan Varr. Off the horse. Hands where we can see them.
Their captain wore no mask. He didn't need one. His head was shaved, half his face was an old burn, and he looked at us the way a butcher looks at a pig.
Brother Caddoc, of the Order's Hounds. The Grand Measurer asked the King to summon you, my lord. He never said you had to arrive.
Officially, you'll be killed by bandits on the King's road. Very sad. Unofficially, you're coming with me. Alive, if you're sensible.
Can I shoot him?
...Yes.
Wren's arrow took him square in the chest. Or it would have. It burst into flame a hand's width from his armour.
Fire ran up his arms. Not the clean gold of Maric's fire. Red, and dirty, and very hot. Six milky stones on his gauntlets lit up, one after another.
Six rings! Lucan, he's a six! There are three sixes alive in the whole kingdom!
Oswin met him blade to blade, frost against fire. For three heartbeats they were even. Then Caddoc's fire roared, and Oswin's frost turned to steam.
My lord, his stones! Seven rings around an eye! They're the Order's, like Penhallow's ring!
Six rings, and not one of them his own.
Born with one, woman. Like any farmer's dog. The Order paid me the other five. One hunt at a time.
The Hounds closed in with nets and chains. They were careful not to shoot me. They weren't careful about anyone else.
Ash dragged down two horses and a Hound, and came back with a crossbow bolt in his shoulder. I felt it in mine, cold as an icicle.
Behind us was the cliff. Below it, the Senn, brown and fast with autumn rain.
Everyone. Into the river.
My lord, I'm wearing a breastplate!
Then take it off on the way down!
Ash went first, with me on his back. Then Wren, and Tamsin, dragging Ilse by the hand. Oswin went last, unbuckling as he fell.
Let the river have him. If it gives him back, I'll be waiting.
The water closed over my head like a door. Ash's fur slipped out of my fingers, and the cold came in.
The last thing I remember is a hand. A thin hand, with long dirty fingers, closing on my collar in the dark.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter sixty-four, coming soon.
